drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 81-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.67, creatinine 0.95-0.97, hemoglobin 13.2-13.3, platelets 302-305, sodium 139, wbc 6.4-7; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 70-75, map 90-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 123-129, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.6
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury ruled out.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.05-1.06, hemoglobin 13.2-13.4, platelets 307-308, sodium 139, wbc 6.5-7; vitals dbp 73-78, heart_rate 70-75, map 92-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 124-129, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury ruled out. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 81-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury ruled out. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
